$comment: Server operations this SDK deliberately does not wrap, each with the reason. test/openapi.test.mjs fails on any operation that is neither called by the SDK nor listed here, and on any entry here that the SDK now implements or the server no longer serves.

operations.GET /v1/wallet/auth/providers: The Cosmos Wallet's own sign-in. It proves who a PERSON is and hands a wallet app a session token; a server holding an API key has no person to sign in.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/auth/oauth/authorize: The Cosmos Wallet's own sign-in — see GET /v1/wallet/auth/providers.
operations.GET /v1/wallet/auth/oauth/callback/{prov: A browser navigation from Google/GitHub/Authentik, not an API call.
operations.GET /v1/wallet/auth/oauth/session/{state: The Cosmos Wallet's own sign-in — see GET /v1/wallet/auth/providers.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/auth/oauth/claim: The Cosmos Wallet's own sign-in — see GET /v1/wallet/auth/providers.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/auth/email/start: The Cosmos Wallet's own sign-in — see GET /v1/wallet/auth/providers.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/auth/email/verify: The Cosmos Wallet's own sign-in — see GET /v1/wallet/auth/providers.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/auth/finish: Needs the wallet's session token AND a signature by the key on the device; a server-side SDK holds neither.
operations.PUT /v1/wallet/backup: Stores a seed box sealed on the device under the person's password; only the wallet that sealed it can produce one.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/recovery/setup: Sponsors the wallet's own SEP-30 enrolment, gated by its sign-in session and a signature by the device key.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/easy-recovery/sessions: The Cosmos Pay Wallet's own recovery flow: the wallet app hands a sealed wallet from a person's old device to their new one (calling with the shared public key); a server-side SDK has no device to recover.
operations.GET /v1/wallet/easy-recovery/sessions/{i: The Cosmos Pay Wallet's own recovery flow; see POST /v1/wallet/easy-recovery/sessions.
operations.POST /v1/wallet/easy-recovery/sessions/{: The Cosmos Pay Wallet's own recovery flow; see POST /v1/wallet/easy-recovery/sessions.
The Cosmos Pay Wallet's own recovery flow; see POST /v1/wallet/easy-recovery/sessions.
operations.GET /v1/payment-links/{id}: The hosted and embedded checkout's keyless read, made from the payer's browser with no API key. The server SDK creates and reads intents (client.paymentIntents); the checkout completes them.
operations.POST /v1/payment-links/{id}/transaction: The hosted and embedded checkout's keyless call that builds the envelope the payer signs, from the payer's browser; see GET /v1/payment-links/{id}.
operations.POST /v1/payment-links/{id}/events: The hosted checkout's keyless report of what the payer did with a wallet, from the payer's browser; see GET /v1/payment-links/{id}.
operations.GET /v1/payment-links/{id}/solana-pay: A Solana Pay transaction request the payer's wallet makes for the checkout, with no API key; see GET /v1/payment-links/{id}.
operations.POST /v1/payment-links/{id}/solana-pay: A Solana Pay transaction request the payer's wallet makes for the checkout, with no API key; see GET /v1/payment-links/{id}.
operations.GET /v1/zk-checkout/config: The private checkout's keyless read of the network's setup, from the payer's browser, which proves the confidential transfers itself. The server SDK reads the same setup with client.privatePayments.config().
operations.GET /v1/zk-checkout/{id}: The private checkout's keyless read of a private payment, from the payer's browser; see GET /v1/zk-checkout/config.
operations.POST /v1/zk-checkout/{id}/confirm: The private checkout's keyless confirmation with the payer's confidential transfers, from the payer's browser; see GET /v1/zk-checkout/config.
operations.GET /.well-known/stellar.toml: SEP-1 discovery on a recovery server, read by SEP-10/SEP-30 clients — a standard with its own client libraries, not this API.
operations.GET /v1/sep10/auth: SEP-10 web authentication on a recovery server: use a SEP-10 client; the credential is a signature by the account, not an API key.
operations.POST /v1/sep30/identity: SEP-30 external authentication on a recovery server (an OIDC ID token for the person who lost their device).
operations.POST /v1/sep30/identity/email/start: SEP-30 external authentication on a recovery server — see POST /v1/sep30/identity.
operations.POST /v1/sep30/identity/email/verify: SEP-30 external authentication on a recovery server — see POST /v1/sep30/identity.
operations.GET /v1/sep30/accounts: SEP-30 account recovery, authenticated with a SEP-10 or identity token from that server — a standard with its own clients.
operations.PUT /v1/sep30/shares/{address}: A recovery server's half of a wallet backup's recovery key, beside SEP-30 and authenticated the same way (a SEP-10 or identity token from that server, not an API key) — a wallet-side concern, not this API.
operations.GET /v1/sep30/shares/{address}: Recovery-key share on a recovery server — see PUT /v1/sep30/shares/{address}.
operations.DELETE /v1/sep30/shares/{address}: Recovery-key share on a recovery server — see PUT /v1/sep30/shares/{address}.
operations.GET /v1/sep30/shares: Every recovery-key share a proven inbox holds on a recovery server — see PUT /v1/sep30/shares/{address}.
